hero.title: Radiation response and tissue repair
hero.copy: The lab uses Drosophila and cancer models to study DNA damage responses, apoptosis, regeneration, loss of heterozygosity, and radiation-modifying drugs.

intro.text: Latest review on radiation-induced cell fate plasticity
Powerful in vivo models for tissue response and regeneration
Drug screens and radiation modulators with translational relevance

research.title: How damaged tissues make choices
research.copy: Ionizing radiation creates a moment of decision for cells and tissues. The lab studies how damage signals, caspases, checkpoints, chromosome state, and tissue context shape whether cells die, survive, change fate, or contribute to regeneration.

areas.title: Cell fate plasticity
areas.copy: Past caspase activity, state switching, and survival after genotoxic stress.

areas.title: Radiation response
areas.copy: Checkpoints, apoptosis, loss of heterozygosity, and organismal recovery.

areas.title: Regeneration
areas.copy: Drosophila models for how epithelia rebuild with precision after injury.

areas.title: Therapeutic discovery
areas.copy: Radiation modulators and translation inhibitors in cancer-relevant models.
